> 吾不敢為主，而為客；不敢進寸，而退尺.

The four characters 哀者勝矣 became an idiom: 哀兵必勝 — the mourning army always wins.

And 說文 gives 哀 in two characters: 哀，閔也.

閔 is grief, and 說文 unpacks 閔 as: 閔，吊者在門也 — the mourner standing at the door.

So 哀 is not "I am sad." It is: I see that someone has died, and I am standing at his door.

Which means 哀者勝矣 is not "the side burning with grievance wins." It is: the side still willing to stand at the door of the dead wins.

## The idiom reverses the chapter

哀兵必勝 as it is used today is a morale doctrine: the oppressed side will turn it around. And morale doctrine works by inflaming soldiers — 項羽 breaking the cauldrons, 韓信 putting his army on dead ground so they fight.

That is the use of 怒, anger.

Chapter 68 said: 善戰者，不怒. The skillful fighter does not get angry.

哀 is the other face of 不怒. It is what a person feels instead of heat when he has understood the cost.

## 主 and 客

主 is the host: the host sets the time and the place.
客: 寄也 — a guest, someone lodging.

So 不敢為主而為客 gives away not the odds but the chair: the one who decides when and where.

不敢進寸，而退尺 — does not dare advance an inch, and retreats a foot. The ratio is one to twelve: the amount yielded is an order of magnitude larger than the amount refused.

## 扔 is not throwing

扔: 因也 — to follow, to meet. 因 is to go along with, to accord.

So 扔無敵 is: meeting it, and there is no enemy to meet.

The four lines of 行無行，攘無臂，扔無敵，執無兵 all have the same structure — an action with its object removed.

行 without ranks; 攘 (rolling up the sleeve) without an arm; meeting without an enemy; holding without a weapon.

That is what an army looks like when it has no counterpart: every motion is present, and nothing is opposing it.

## 禍莫大於輕敵

The greatest calamity is underestimating the enemy. 輕敵幾喪吾寶 — it nearly costs me the treasure.

The treasure is chapter 67's 慈. Underestimating the opponent is not a tactical error; it is what happens when the protection has lapsed and the calculation has taken over.

## 抗兵相若，哀者勝矣

Two armies raised against each other, matched — the one that is 哀 wins.

相若 is "roughly equal." The chapter is not promising that weakness beats strength. It is saying: when everything else cancels out, what decides is whether one side still remembers the dead.

That is a narrow claim, and it is the only one the chapter makes.

## Why this follows 68

68 removed the four surfaces — display, heat, counterpart, height.
69 gives the interior state that makes the removal possible: standing at the door.

You cannot stop being angry by deciding to stop. You stop when you have stood at the door and seen what the anger costs.

## A test

Take a fight you are in, and ask whether you are 主 or 客 — who is setting the time and the place. Most people who believe they are being patient are actually the host, and holding the chair is what keeps the conflict running.

Then ask the second question: have you stood at the door, or are you only angry?
